Another alternative for the more technically inclined is to...

  • run a Nextcloud instance from home and federate with others to distribute the information. This is extremely resilient for a few reasons.
    • It runs over https so it pretty much can't be blocked by any network that communicates with the Internet.
    • If you federate your server with others, the data will be duplicated and much harder to track down and erase.
    • You can also incorporate automatic mirroring to other cloud services like Dropbox and Google Drive.
  • Set up IFTT to automatically push your video to Nexcloud or other cloud services so that you don't have to mess with it in a pinch.
    • If the cops take your phone... it's busy uploading in the background and even if they manage to get access (it should be encrypted) and delete the local copy... the backup is already sent.

No, but it requires computer skills. Basic Linux skills and likely the ability to run virtual machines.

I run a VSphere Server, but any old computer (down to a P4 but I'd suggest a dual core and up) will do.

This is what the web interface looks like. It's basically like running a private version of Dropbox but a lot more powerful. You can add other users and groups. You can make encrypted link, time expiring links, upload only folders, save file versions based on revisions etc. It has desktop clients and phone clients. It also has tons of plugins. Calendar, contacts, photo albums, pdf viewer, document editor, group document editor, video conferencing and a lot more.

The setup is very straightforward on Ubuntu server but you should have a basic understanding of the Linux command line before attempting to set it up. Here's a few resources to help you out. You can practice in a virtual machine using Virtualbox or VMWare Player... both of which are free.
